  ▸ All columns                                                            a
▾ How it was measured                                                      m
  • The speed is the engine running on its own, with nothing recording it,
    at a context of 530 tokens.
  • Each part was timed inside the real run, recorded with nsys.
  • The recording was repeated 3 times; the parts agree within 0.2% (the
    rule allows 1%).
  • Recording slowed the run by 11.5% (the limit is 5%).
  • The part times still stand, because the repeated recordings agree; the
    idle time is shown as at most what the unrecorded run leaves.
  • The limit is the time to read every byte this step needs once, at this
    GPU's measured memory speed (962.0 GB/s); no real run can be faster.
  • The gains share out the lost time by how long each part takes; they add
    up to the limit, but they are not promised speed-ups.
  • A part with no limit of its own counts all of its time as lost.
  • No repeat runs of this exact setup yet, so how much these numbers vary
    from run to run is not known.
▾ Machine and engine                                                       e
  • GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 962.0 GB/s memory speed (measured on this
    GPU (native CUDA read probe, 2026-11-09)).
  • Engine: llama.cpp build 11571 (097cf33d9), installed 2026-11-09 · the
    pin b11571 (097cf33d9), set 2026-10-12.
  • Upstream: build 097cf33d9; latest not checked (the last check failed:
    HTTPError: HTTP Error 403: rate limit exceeded).
  • Weights: GGUF Q4_K+Q6_K.
  • Toolchain: CUDA 13.0, GPU driver 595.58.03, Nsight Compute 2025.3.1,
    Nsight Systems 2026.5.2, PyTorch unknown.
  • How parts were timed: in-model.
▾ Words used here                                                          w
  • tok/s: Tokens a second: how many words (or pieces of words) the model
    writes each second. Higher is faster.
  • limit: The fastest this GPU allows for this model: the time to move
    every byte the step needs once at the GPU's memory speed (or, for heavy
    maths, at its top compute speed). A real run is always slower.
  • ms: Milliseconds: thousandths of a second.
  • context: How many tokens of conversation the model already holds when it
    writes the next one. More context means more to read.
  • part: One piece of the model's work in each step, such as the feed-
    forward or attention layers, or the time between GPU steps.
  • time: How long this part takes now, in each token (or each step of
    several streams, or each prompt).
  • share: This part's share of the lost time: of all the time the run takes
    beyond the limit, how much is in this part.
  • gain: What this part would give back if it ran at its own limit: its
    share of the distance from the measured speed to the limit.
  • cumulative: The speed with this part and every part above it fixed.
  • time lost: A part's time now, less its time at the limit.
  • chip best: The fastest this kind of work can run on this GPU by any
    method, not only the engine's.
  • % of peak: How much of the GPU's top memory speed a part reaches while
    it runs.
  • GB/s: Gigabytes a second: how fast memory is read.
  • idle time: Time between GPU kernels, when the GPU waits for the next
    piece of work.
  • recording: A tool that watches the GPU and notes when every kernel
    starts and ends. Watching slows the run a little.
  • untraced: The run with no recording tool attached: the speed the engine
    really has.
  • repeat runs: The same setup run several times, so a later change can be
    told apart from normal variation.
  • quant: How the model's numbers are stored: fewer bits per number means
    less to read and a faster step, at some cost in accuracy.
  • KV cache: What the model keeps about earlier tokens (keys and values),
    read again for every new token.
  • attention: The part of the model that looks back at earlier tokens.
  • feed-forward: The largest part of each layer: two big matrix steps on
    every token.
  • engine: The program that runs the model (llama.cpp, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM
    or tinygrad).
  • build: The engine's version. The pin is the version BoltBeam was last
    checked against; upstream is the newest release.
  • toolchain: The GPU driver and libraries the engine was built with.
